anomaly_signals.detail: 448 errors out of 1000 spans — 44.8% error rate. Likely the primary blast radius entry point of the cascading failure, rejecting or failing nearly half of all requests.
256 errors out of 1000 spans — 25.6% error rate. Severe downstream impact from postgres-auth degradation; auth failures propagate upstream to api-gateway.
108 errors out of 1000 spans — 10.8% error rate. Database-layer failures driving auth-service and api-gateway error cascade.
147 errors out of 404 spans — 36.4% error rate. Over a third of payment transactions failing, posing direct business/revenue risk.
76 errors out of 865 spans (8.8% error rate) combined with system-wide p99 latency of 11,605 ms strongly suggests LLM timeouts or overload contributing to tail latency.
37 GenAI token truncation events detected across the batch. Responses may be incomplete, degrading agent/workflow output quality.
27 GenAI tool call failures alongside 17 tool-executor error spans. Agent tool use is unreliable; tasks dependent on external tools will produce degraded or incorrect results.
10 errors out of 470 spans (2.1%). Secondary downstream effect of LLM and tool-executor instability.

recommended_action: Immediately investigate postgres-auth stability (connection pool exhaustion, disk I/O, or query timeouts) as the likely cascade origin — restoring it should relieve auth-service and api-gateway error rates. In parallel, cap or circuit-break payments-service retries to prevent revenue loss, throttle llm-gemini request concurrency to reduce tail latency and token truncations, and review tool-executor failure logs to identify which tools are flapping.
summary: A cascading failure is actively propagating from the database layer (postgres-auth) through auth-service and into api-gateway, causing a system-wide 14% error rate and p99 latency of ~11.6 seconds. Payments-service is concurrently failing at 36%, and the GenAI layer is compounding the incident with 37 token truncations and 27 tool failures.
